title: TypeError: dot() got an unexpected keyword argument 'trans_b'
body: I am integrating the Triton version of Flash Attention into a GPT-like model. Calling flash_attn_triton.flash_attn_func with half-precision CUDA query, key, and value tensors fails with `TypeError: dot() got an unexpected keyword argument 'trans_b'`. The attention code and a complete test example are included.

symptoms_visible: Running the Triton Flash Attention call in my GPT-like attention module raises `TypeError: dot() got an unexpected keyword argument 'trans_b'`.
N0.label: N0 trans_b API error reported

symptoms_visible: After changing the Flash Attention source to `qk += tl.dot(q, tl.trans(k))`, both the latest stable package and the available nightly raise `AttributeError: module 'triton.language' has no attribute 'trans'`.
N1.label: N1 packaged builds lack explicit transpose API

symptoms_visible: Installing the cloned Triton source with `pip install -e .` stops while compiling `LLVMIRTranslation.cpp` because `<filesystem>` cannot be found.
Another installation attempt stops while preparing the cmake package with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'skbuild'`.
N2_x.label: N2_x source build failure aftermath

symptoms_visible: The source build still stops at the missing `<filesystem>` header on my Ubuntu 18.04 GCC environment.
The installation has also repeatedly stopped while downloading or building, eventually stopping around 91%.
N3.label: N3 compiler environment collected

symptoms_visible: With gcc/g++ 9, I can install Triton from source and run the Triton version of Flash Attention successfully.
N_terminal.label: terminal source build and Flash Attention working

question_patterns: After updating the attention source, what error do you get and which Triton builds have you tested?
Please try the updated source and report the exact exception and the Triton package channel you used.
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I tried both the most updated stable Triton version and the available nightly. After changing the line to `qk += tl.dot(q, tl.trans(k))`, I get `AttributeError: module 'triton.language' has no attribute 'trans'`.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: The explicit transpose works with my installed package and the Flash Attention test now runs successfully.
The stable package lacks the attribute, but I have not tested the nightly package.

solution.intent: Update the outdated Flash Attention kernel syntax by replacing the removed `trans_b` argument with an explicit transpose of the second dot operand.
solution.concrete_example: On current Triton master, replace a call such as `tl.dot(q, k, trans_b=True)` with `tl.dot(q, tl.trans(k))`, following the fused-attention tutorial.
solution.inference_hint: The initial TypeError indicates that the bundled Flash Attention kernel is calling a Triton dot API whose `trans_b` keyword is no longer accepted. The reporter supplied the exception and code, while mapping it to the updated explicit-transpose API is engineer inference.

edges.comment: Issue opening and c0-c2, reporter conceptofmind: the maintainer recommends explicit `tl.trans`; the reporter edits the kernel and reports that the stable and available nightly packages do not expose that API. The source edit is recorded as volunteered information on N1 because the reporter reports it alongside the requested test result. The direction remains valid for current source, so this is not a falsified solution.

solution.intent: Install the current Triton master from source because the available stable and nightly packages are too old to provide the explicit transpose API.
solution.concrete_example: Clone the Triton repository, enter `triton/python`, install the cmake build dependency, and run `pip install -e .`.

edges.comment: c3-c9, reporter conceptofmind: installing current source is the correct direction, but the unqualified attempt on the reporter's existing Ubuntu 18.04 toolchain fails with the pasted `<filesystem>` and skbuild errors. Repeating the same install without addressing the compiler is a known failed move.

question_patterns: Which operating system and compiler are you using for the source build?
Can you check the compiler family and version used when the `<filesystem>` include fails?
clarifications.user_answer_in_this_oncall: I am pretty sure it is GCC on Ubuntu 18.04. I will have to check the exact compiler version when I get back.

counterfactual_candidates.answer: I am already using GCC 11 on Ubuntu 22.04, and a small C++17 program including `<filesystem>` compiles successfully.
It is the default GCC installation on Ubuntu 18.04, but I do not have the exact patch version yet.

edges.comment: c11-c12, reporter conceptofmind: the maintainer asks for the compiler version after reading the raw `<filesystem>` build failure. The reporter can only say that it is GCC on Ubuntu 18.04 and does not yet provide an exact version.

solution.intent: Use a compiler with C++17 support, then install current Triton from source and keep the Flash Attention kernel's explicit `tl.trans` form.
solution.concrete_example: Ubuntu 18.04 defaults to an older GCC that cannot build this source. Install and select a newer gcc/g++ such as gcc/g++ 9, rebuild Triton from source, retain `tl.dot(q, tl.trans(k))`, and rerun the Flash Attention example.
solution.inference_hint: The maintainer infers from Ubuntu 18.04 and the missing `<filesystem>` header that the default GCC 7.5 toolchain lacks the required C++17 support. This compiler problem blocks installation of the source version needed for `tl.trans`; it is not the cause of the original `trans_b` runtime API error.

edges.comment: c14-c17, reporter conceptofmind: the maintainer explains that Ubuntu 18.04's default GCC is too old and recommends a newer gcc/clang. The reporter upgrades to gcc/g++ 9, installs Triton from source, and confirms that the Triton Flash Attention implementation runs.

satisfaction_conditions: Must identify the original failure as an API mismatch in the Flash Attention kernel: its `tl.dot` call uses the obsolete `trans_b` keyword and should use an explicit transpose with current Triton source.
Must distinguish the later source-build failure from the original runtime error: Ubuntu 18.04's old default GCC lacks the C++17 support needed to compile the current source.
Must recommend a C++17-capable compiler, installation of current Triton source, and the explicit `tl.trans` dot form rather than claiming the old stable or stale nightly package supports it.
Must not merely repeat `pip install -e .` under the unchanged old compiler, because that attempt already stopped at the missing `<filesystem>` header.
Must ask the reporter to rerun the Flash Attention example after rebuilding and only treat the issue as resolved once it runs successfully.

persona_hint.experience_level: Moderately technical ML developer who can modify Python and Triton kernel source, manage CUDA environments, clone repositories, and paste compiler traces, but needs guidance diagnosing native compiler and packaging requirements.
persona_hint.communication_style: Polite, cooperative, and concise; reports exact exceptions and command output, follows recommendations, and returns with verification results.
